findings.current: “So you were planning this from the very beginning.”
findings.rationale: The Korean question ending asks whether the Skeleton King intended this all along.
findings.replacement: “Just as I thought. Was that your plan from the start?”

findings.current: It seems I underestimated you—or rather, you.
findings.defect: The shift from addressing a group to addressing the Skeleton King alone is unintelligible in English.
findings.rationale: 너희 is plural; 자네 singles out the Skeleton King.
findings.replacement: It seems I underestimated all of you… No, I underestimated you.
findings.source: 나는 너희를…… 아니 자네를 과소평가하고 있던 모양이야.

findings.current: With an incantationless spell that came as naturally as breathing, Morgoth’s strike transcended the limits of Blink magic and slammed into the Skeleton King’s back.
findings.defect: The draft makes the strike, rather than Morgoth’s use of Blink, transcend the spell’s limits.
findings.rationale: The source describes Morgoth appearing through an extraordinary use of Blink before his blow lands.
findings.replacement: Morgoth cast a wordless spell as naturally as breathing, pushed Blink magic past its limits, and appeared to strike the Skeleton King in the back.
findings.source: 무영창 주문과 함께, 블링크 마법의 한계를 초월하여 나타난 모르고스의 일격이 스켈레톤 킹의 등줄기를 후려쳤다.

findings.current:
they would surely have thought of two words:

The end.
findings.defect: 종말 is one word of two Korean characters, not two words; “The end” also weakens its apocalyptic sense.
findings.rationale: The source names an end-of-the-world event, followed by images of the world’s and all living things’ final moments.
findings.replacement:
they would surely have thought of one word:

Apocalypse.
findings.source:
분명 두 글자를 떠올렸을 것이다.

종말(終末).

summary: The draft preserves the scene’s main events but changes a question into a statement, loses a deliberate shift in address, and misattributes the limit-breaking magic.
